messages:
maria: Quick one — UX for automatic fallback decisions. Do we want a compact 'Why did this fallback?' card on route pages, or keep it only in the audit logs?

kenji: Compact card on route page = yes. Most users will ask "why" first. Card should show trigger type + policy name + brief matched condition. :thumbsup:

maria: Sketch idea: top line = trigger (e.g. 5xx spike / latency p99 / quota breach), second line = policy id, then an expand to show matched thresholds and a sample decision payload.

samir: Agree, but we must avoid leaking PII in the card. Any request fields in decision payload must be scrubbed or redacted by default.

ellie: Also think about retention. For debugging we want 90d, but for audits some customers want 1y. Maybe policy-level retention override?

prateek: +1 on per-customer override. But that will affect storage/costs. We should surface estimated storage impact in the Console when they change it.

ops-bot: deploy: audit pipeline for fallback-decisions v1 deployed to staging.

kenji: UX question: should we include a "replay decision" button that simulates traffic and shows whether the policy would have fired? Could be helpful for SREs.

maria: I like replay but it must be safe & sampled. It can't re-run customer requests live. Maybe a simulator that replays synthetic requests using recorded signals (latency histogram, error rates) to reproduce the match.

samir: For API integration — do we want a response header when a fallback happens? e.g. `X-Redwood-Fallback: true; reason=5xx_spike; policy=autofallback_v2`

prateek: That would help downstream observability, but it might surface internal policy names to clients. Security concern. Maybe an internal-only header that we strip before forwarding, and an event posted to the audit stream.

ellie: Also think sampling. Store full decision payload for sampled requests (1-5% by default) and store metadata (trigger type, policy id, timestamp) for all fallbacks. That balances debuggability and cost.

maria: Good idea. So small metadata always, full payload sampled. Need to document how to opt into full capture for a route (owner override).

kenji: Telemetry/metrics: add a per-route fallback counter, broken down by trigger and outcome (succeeded fallback / rollback). Expose in route dashboard and route-level alerting.

samir: One more API thing: operators will want to query fallback history via the internal API. Add filter by time window, trigger, and operator id. We should return anonymized payloads unless requestor has permission.

ops-bot: incident: FYI - last night a tenant hit autofallback due to a deploy causing 502s. We logged ~8k fallback events, sampling at 2%. Engineers are analyzing.

maria: Action items: (1) UX: prototype compact 'Why' card + replay button mockups (kenji), (2) Backend: implement metadata + sampled payload retention with per-customer retention override (samir/prateek), (3) Security: ensure scrubber for PII and internal-only header behavior (ellie).

kenji: I'll put a short Figma mock in #design later today.

samir: I'll draft the retention cost calc for pricing page.

ellie: I'll write the scrubber spec + list of fields to redact.

maria: Cool. If no objections we'll sync tomorrow in design huddle. :eyes:

prateek: No objections from me. Also flagging that quota-triggered fallbacks need special UX because customers might think we silently throttle them. We should show "quota" vs "health" badges differently.

maria: Good call — add badge distinction to mock.

kenji: noted.

maria: Thanks all.
